title: Joe Jordan gets him into Ferman Tapp's band and the union
summary: Sick with a stomach problem and wanting a New York card, Thomas left Henderson. Jordan sent him to banjoist Ferman Tapp, which got him into the union; he worked there three months.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Right. Well, how, why do you leave Smack and go with Fermin Tapp?
I had a little trouble. I was sick in those days.
You had what?
I was pretty sick in those days.
Oh, were you, with your stomach?
Stomach, yeah. And, I wanted to stay around town. Also, I wanted to get a New York card.
Yeah and they were going out of town?

Yeah and I wanted to get the New York card, you know. So, Joe Jordan, whom I have tremendous respect for, I didn't know him before. I knew his name and I'm sure he didn't know me and we did some things at ... later on, ... respect for him. So one night he talks to me, he says, You Joe Thomas? I says, "Yes, I'm Joe Thomas." He says, I"m Joe Jordan. I said, Yes, I know. ...
Go on. Carry on.
Well, ...
Oh, you want me to switch off?
No, keep it there. Leave it right there. So he said you need a job. I said, I sure do.
Yeah. Piano, leader, and arranger.
JT (2 of 1) 98

He said I know a guy who needs a trumpet player. Yeah? I tell you what you do. You want to get your card, don't you? Yeah, I sure do. I know a fellow by the name of Ferman Tapp that has a band ... at one time, according to what the people say, you pay more money than any body in Harlem. I don't know. Anyhow, he said, you go over and see this fellow and you hang out? I said, No, I don't hang out. ... Don't hang out. You go on and make your deal and I'll come by and see you or you come by to see me. He say, Can you read the music. I said, Don't you worry about it. That's where I got in the union through Joe Jordan.
And Ferman Tapp was a banjo player?
Yeah, he played banjo and guitar. A very fine musician, too.
Well, ...
You know about Joe Jordan?
Joe Jordan.
He's a tremendous musician. OK.
No, I really don't know about him.
Well, I'll tell you about him in another story.
And we worked down there for, I worked there for the three month period. We go down there sometimes at 9 o'clock at night and leave at 12 o'clock on Sunday. WOW.
